grades.quote: Apart from transfer operations described in the previous paragraph, all other floating-point operations on narrower _n_ -bit operations, _n_ <FLEN, check if the input operands are correctly NaN-boxed, i.e., all upper FLEN- _n_ bits are 1. If so, the _n_ least-significant bits of the input are used as the input value, otherwise the input value is treated as an _n_ -bit canonical NaN.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary context on when an operand is treated as NaN, but gives no FEQ, FLT, or FLE comparison results or exception-flag behavior.

grades.quote: RISC-V applies NaN boxing to scalar results and checks for NaN boxing when a floating-point operation --- even a vector-scalar operation --- consumes a value from a scalar floating-point register. If the value is properly NaN-boxed, its least significant bits are used as the operand, otherwise it is treated as if it were the canonical QNaN.
grades.reason: Explains auxiliary NaN-input handling through boxing, but does not explain comparison outcomes or exception flags for FEQ, FLT, and FLE.
